﴿And indeed, we are a cautious (jami') multitude.﴾ Al-Nakha'i, al-Aswad ibn Yazid, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umar, and the rest of the reciters of Kufa, along with Ibn 'Amir and al-Dahhak, recited ḥādhirūn (حاذِرُونَ) with an alif. This is the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas, and the preference of Abu 'Ubayd. The others recited ḥadhirūn (حذرون) without an alif. Both are dialectal forms (lughatan).

Some people said: ḥādhirūn means: equipped and armed, bearing weapons, people of strength and horses (or army). And ḥadhirūn means: alert and watchful. Al-Farra' said: The ḥādhir is the one who causes you to be wary, while the ḥadhar (wary) is the created one who is cautious, so that he does not meet except with caution. And al-ḥadhar is avoiding a thing out of fear of it.

Shumayt ibn 'Ijlan recited ḥādirūn (حادرون) with an undotted dal. Al-Farra' said: It means tall, from the abundance of weapons. From it is said of a great eye: ḥadra, and of one who is swollen: ḥādir. Imru' al-Qays said:

And an eye for which there is a large swelling,
Its eyelids pour out tears from behind.

[Lisan al-Arab: 4/15.]

So We expelled them from gardens, springs, and treasures. Mujahid said: He called them treasures because they were not spent in obedience to Allah, glorified is He. ﴿And a noble station﴾, meaning a good assembly. ﴿Thus it was,﴾ as We have described. ﴿And We made the Children of Israel inherit them.﴾ ﴿So they pursued them at sunrise,﴾ meaning they caught up with them at the time of sunrise, which is its brightening. ﴿And when the two groups saw each other,﴾ meaning they faced each other such that each party saw the other. Yahya, al-A'mash, Hamza and Khalaf read tarā'ā (تراءى) with a kasra on the ra', while the rest read it with a fatḥa.

The companions of Musa said: ﴿Indeed, we are going to be overtaken,﴾ meaning: overtaken. Al-A'raj and 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr recited mudrakūn (لمدّركون) with a shaddah on the dal. The preferred recitation is that of the common reciters, like His saying: ﴿until, when drowning overtook him﴾ [Yunus: 90].

Musa said, trusting in the promise of Allah: ﴿No! Indeed, they will not overtake you. Indeed, my Lord is with me; He will guide me.﴾ That is, to the path of salvation. So We revealed to Musa: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff.﴾

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Dhanjawi informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Yaqtini informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Aqili informed us, saying: Safwan ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hamza and 'Abd Allah ibn Salam narrated to me, that when Musa reached the sea, he said: "O You who preceded everything, and who brought everything into being, and who exists after everything, make for us a way out!" So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff,﴾ and it split (fa-infalaqa), meaning it was cleft. ﴿And each part was like a great mountain,﴾ meaning each portion of water was like a huge mountain.

Ibn Jurayj and others said: When Musa reached the sea, the wind raged, and the sea was throwing up waves like mountains. Yusha' said to him: "O speaker of Allah, where were you commanded? Pharaoh has overtaken us, and the sea is in front of us!" Musa said: "Here." So Yusha' plunged into the water, and the sea receded until the hoof of his horse was reached by the water. The one who was concealing his faith said: "O speaker of Allah, where were you commanded?" He said: "Here." So he pulled his horse's reins until the foam flew from its jaws, then he forced it into the sea, and the water was split. The people tried to do the same but could not. Musa did not know what to do, so Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff,﴾ and he struck it with his staff, and it split. Behold, the man was standing on his horse, and his saddle-cloth and saddle were not wet.

﴿And We brought the others near there,﴾ meaning the people of Pharaoh. He says: We drew them near to destruction and brought them forward to the sea.

﴿And We rescued Musa and all who were with him,﴾ ﴿then We drowned the others,﴾ Pharaoh and his people. ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾

Muqatil said: None of the people of Egypt believed except Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh, Khurbil the believer, and Maryam, daughter of Musa'a, who pointed to the bones of Yusuf.

﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Almighty, the Most Merciful.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 26, verses 34–68:

Pharaoh said to the chiefs around him: ﴿Indeed, this is a skilled sorcerer. He intends to drive you out of your land with his sorcery. So what do you advise?﴾ They said: ﴿Put him off, and his brother, and send heralds into the cities to bring you every skilled sorcerer.﴾ So the sorcerers were gathered for an appointed time on a known day, and it was the Day of Adornment (yawm al-zina).

Ibn 'Abbas said: That day coincided with a Saturday, the first day of the year, and it was the day of Nawruz (the Persian New Year).

Ibn Zayd said: Their gathering for the appointed time was in Alexandria. It is also said: the tail of the serpent reached beyond the lake that day.

And it was said to the people: ﴿Will you gather, so that you may watch what the two parties do, and so that we may follow the sorcerers if they are the victors?﴾ It was said that they meant this in mockery, and by "the sorcerers" they meant Musa, Harun and their people.

When the sorcerers came, they said to Pharaoh: ﴿Will we surely have a reward if we are the victors?﴾ He said: ﴿Yes, and you will then be among those brought near.﴾ Musa said to them: ﴿Throw what you are going to throw.﴾ So they threw their ropes and their staffs, and said: ﴿By the might of Pharaoh, we are surely the victors.﴾ Then Musa threw his staff, and behold, it swallowed what they had falsely produced. So the sorcerers fell down prostrating, and said: ﴿We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun.﴾ He said: ﴿Do you believe in Him before I give you permission? Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic. You will soon know. I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you all.﴾ They said: ﴿No harm. Indeed, we are returning to our Lord. We hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins, because we are the first of the believers.﴾ And We revealed to Musa: ﴿Travel by night with My servants; indeed, you will be pursued.﴾ (That is, Pharaoh and his people will pursue you.)

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Lu'lu' narrated to us, saying: al-Haytham ibn Khalaf informed us, saying: al-Dawraqi narrated to us, from Hajjaj ibn Jurayj, regarding this verse, that he said: Allah, glorified is He, revealed to Musa: "Gather the Children of Israel, every four households in one house. Then slaughter lambs and strike their blood upon your property, for I will command the angels so that they will not enter a house upon whose door there is blood. I will command them to kill the firstborn of the family of Pharaoh, from among their own persons and their wealth. Then bake unleavened bread, for it is quicker for you. Then travel by night with My servants until you reach the sea, and My command will come to you." He did so. When they woke in the morning, Pharaoh said: "This is the deed of Musa and his people. They have killed our firstborn from among ourselves and our wealth." So he sent into his affair one million and five hundred thousand crowned kings, with each king having a thousand. Pharaoh went out in the great throne.

Then Pharaoh sent heralds into the cities, meaning the police, to gather the sorcerers, and he said to them: ﴿Indeed, these are a small band (shirdhima).﴾ A shirdhima of anything is its small remnant. From it is the saying of the rajiz (a poet of the rajaz meter):

The winter came, and my shirt is worn out,
Remnants, at which the one who is anxious for it laughs.

[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 14/27.]

Ibn Mas'ud said: These "small band" numbered six hundred and seventy thousand.

Abu Bakr al-Kharimi informed us, saying: Abu Hamid al-A'mash informed us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak al-Mukhrami narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, regarding this verse, that he said: The companions of Musa were six hundred thousand.

Its eyelids pour out tears from behind.

[Lisan al-Arab: 4/15.]

So he pulled his horse's reins until the foam flew from its jaws, then he forced it into the sea, and the water was split. The people tried to do the same but could not. Musa did not know what to do, so Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff,﴾ and he struck it with his staff, and it split. Behold, the man was standing on his horse, and his saddle-cloth and saddle were not wet.

﴿And We brought the others near there,﴾ meaning the people of Pharaoh. He says: We drew them near to destruction and brought them forward to the sea.

﴿And We rescued Musa and all who were with him,﴾ ﴿then We drowned the others,﴾ Pharaoh and his people. ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾

﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Almighty, the Most Merciful.﴾

And recite to them the account of Ibrahim, when he said to his father and his people: "What do you worship?" They said: "We worship idols, and we remain devoted to them." ﴿What do you worship?﴾

Some scholars said: They said "fa-nazallu" (so we remain) because they worshipped them by day and not by night.

He said: "Do they hear you when you call (on them)?" ﴿Do they hear you when you call (on them)?﴾ The common reading (qira'a) is with a fatha on the ya', meaning: do they hear your supplication? Qatada read yusmi'unakum with a damma on the ya', meaning: do they make you hear? ﴿Or do they benefit you or harm you?﴾ They said: "No, but we found our fathers doing thus." ﴿They said: No, but we found our fathers doing thus.﴾

In this verse there is a demonstration that religion is established only by proof, and that blind imitation (taqlid) in it is invalid.

He said: "Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers, the ancients? ﴿Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers, the ancients?﴾ For they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds." ﴿For they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds.﴾ He used the singular "enemy" because the meaning of the statement is: every object of worship you have is an enemy to me, if I were to worship them on the Day of Resurrection, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They will deny their worship of them and will be opposed to them﴾.

Al-Farra' said: this is an inversion (maqlub); he meant: "I am their enemy," because whoever you oppose opposes you.

Then He said: "except the Lord of the worlds," which is in the accusative by way of exception, meaning: they are an enemy to me, and what is not worshipped by me, except the Lord of the worlds, for I worship Him. This is what al-Farra' said. It was also said that it means "but" (lakin). Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: meaning the matter is with the Lord of the worlds.

Then He described Him, saying: ﴿Who created me, and it is He who guides me﴾. He informed that the true guide is the Creator, and there is no guide other than Him.

The people of language (ahl al-lisan) said: ﴿Who created me﴾ in this world upon His natural disposition (fitra), ﴿and it is He who guides me﴾ in the Hereafter to His Garden.

﴿And who feeds me and gives me drink﴾, meaning: who provides for me and nurtures me.

Abu al-'Abbas ibn 'Ata' said: meaning He feeds me whatever food He wills, and gives me to drink whatever drink He wills.

Muhammad ibn Kathir al-'Abdi said: I accompanied Sufyan al-Thawri in Mecca for a long time, and he would sip from Saturday to Saturday a handful of sand.

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: I heard Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Shah say: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Hamdan say: I heard al-Hajjaj ibn 'Abd al-Karim say:

I left Balkh seeking Ibrahim ibn Adham, and I found him in Hims in a kiln which he was heating. I greeted him and asked about his condition, and he returned my greeting and asked me about my condition and the condition of my relatives. I stayed with him that day, and he said: "Perhaps your soul urges you towards some food?" I said: "Yes." So he took ashes and dust, mixed them together, and ate them. Then he turned his face towards me and recited:

"Mix the dust with the ash and eat it,
and restrain the soul from standing in the place of asking.

If you wish to be humbled by disgrace,
then throw away what the hands of men contain."

So I left him and remained for days without entering upon him, and my longing for him grew intense. I entered upon him and was with him, but he did not speak a word. I said to him: "Why do you not speak?" He said:

"Silence in speech is forbidden, for it is the cause of perdition,
and speech contains the mines of calamities.

So when you speak, be mindful of your Lord,
and when you are silent, count your body as dead."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "﴿Who feeds me﴾ without food, and ﴿gives me drink﴾ without drink." Its figurative meaning is: He satisfies me and quenches me without any intermediary, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I pass the night being fed by my Lord and given drink by Him."

This is shown by the hadith of the water-carrier in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), when he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) recite for three days: ﴿There is no creature on earth but that its provision is upon Allah﴾, and he threw away his waterskin. Then someone came to him in a dream with a cup of the drink of Paradise and gave him to drink.

Anas said: He lived after that for more than twenty years, not eating or drinking according to his desire.

Ali ibn Qadim said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Na'm would not eat more than once a month. This reached al-Hajjaj, who summoned him, placed him in a house, and locked its door. He opened it after fifteen days, not doubting that he had died, and found him standing and praying. He said: "O wicked one, you pray without ablution!" He replied: "Only one who eats and drinks needs ablution, and I am in the state of purity into which you placed me in this house."

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Naysaburi say: I heard Abu Nasr Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah al-Isfahani say: I heard Abu Sa'id al-Kharraz in Mecca say: I was hungry in Tarsus, and my hunger intensified, so I sat on the bank of the river and placed my feet in the water, and I was called: "Are you weary of your hunger? Take the satiety of eternity."

He said: So he lived after that for years without desiring food or drink, yet whenever he wished to eat or drink, he was able to.

It reached me that a woman was taken captive from Aleppo to the Byzantines in the days of Sayf al-Dawla 'Ali ibn Hamdan. She escaped from them and walked two hundred farsakh without eating anything. She came to Sayf al-Dawla, and he said to her: "How were you able to walk, and how did you live without food?" She said: "Whenever I was hungry or exhausted, I recited ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ three times, and I was satisfied, quenched and strengthened."

I heard Abu al-Qasim say: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Nasrabadi say: I heard Abu Bakr al-Shibli say: There is a subtlety in bread that satisfies you, not the bread itself. Had He willed, He would have left that subtlety in you so that you would not need bread.

Dhu al-Nun al-Misri said: "He feeds me the food of love and gives me to drink the drink of love." Then he recited:

"The drink of love is the best of drinks,
and every other drink is a mirage."

I heard Ibn Habib say: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Jurjani say: I heard al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiyya al-Damghani say [in the second copy there is an addition: Abu al-Qasim said: he heard my father say: I heard 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Warraq say: I heard my uncle say]: I heard my uncle say: I heard Abu Yazid al-Bistami say: Indeed Allah has a drink called the drink of love, which He has stored up for His most excellent servants. When they drink it, they become intoxicated; when they are intoxicated, they become senseless; when they are senseless, they fly; when they fly, they arrive; and when they arrive, they are joined. They are ﴿in a seat of truth, in the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful﴾.

Al-Junayd said: People will be gathered all naked, except those who wore the garment of piety; and hungry, except those who ate the food of gnosis (ma'rifa); and thirsty, except those who drank the drink of love.

﴿And when I am ill﴾: Ibrahim (peace be upon him) attributed the illness to himself, though it is from Allah the Exalted, because his people regarded it as a defect, so he employed good manners. Similar to this is the story of al-Khidr, when he said: ﴿So I intended to damage it﴾, and he said: ﴿So your Lord intended that they should reach their maturity﴾.

﴿And it is He who cures me﴾, meaning: heals me. It is related that Abu Bakr al-Warraq passed by a physician who was giving medicines to people, so he stopped by him and said: "Does your medicine do two things?" He said: "And what are they?" He said: "Reverse the decree of a judge and bring about the cure of one who cures?" He said: "No." He said: "Then it is not [anything]."

Ja'far al-Sadiq said: ﴿And when I am ill with sins, He cures me with repentance﴾. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/111.]

Samir ibn 'Abd Allah [in the second copy: Abu 'Abd Allah said]: When the endurance of people's company makes me ill, He cures me by remembering Him and by intimacy with Him.

﴿And it is He who causes me to die, then gives me life﴾. Here "thumma" (then) is used to indicate a break and a delay.

The people of language and allusion said: He causes me to die by justice and gives me life by grace; He causes me to die by disobedience and gives me life by obedience; He causes me to die by separation and gives me life by reunion; He causes me to die by abandonment and gives me life by success; He causes me to die by wealth and gives me life by it; He causes me to die by ignorance and gives me life by knowledge.

﴿And who I hope will forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment﴾. The common reading (qira'a) is in the singular (khati'a).

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hanash related to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yazid related to us, saying: Rawh related to us, from Abu al-Yaqzan, who said: al-Hakam al-Sulami related to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan recite: "and who I hope will forgive me my sins on the Day of Judgment." He said: "It was not a single sin, but it was sins."

Mujahid and Muqatil said: they are his saying ﴿I am sick﴾, and his saying ﴿Rather, the largest of them did it﴾, and his saying to Sarah "She is my sister," al-Hasan added, and his saying about the stars ﴿This is my lord﴾.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Shadhan related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Thabit al-Hariri related to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us, saying: Abu Khalid related to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, from 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: O Messenger of Allah, 'Abd Allah ibn Jud'an used to feed the guest, maintain the ties of kinship, and free the captive; will that benefit him? He said: "No, for he never once said: 'O Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment.'"

This statement by Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is an argument against his people, and an announcement that none is fit for divinity except one who does these acts.

﴿My Lord, grant me wisdom (hukm)﴾, which is the clear explanation of a thing according to what wisdom requires. Muqatil said: understanding and knowledge; al-Kalbi said: prophethood.

﴿And join me with the righteous﴾, with those before me among the prophets in rank and station. Ibn 'Abbas said: with the people of Paradise.

﴿And make for me a tongue of truth among the later ones﴾, meaning: a good remembrance, a praiseworthy reputation, and general acceptance among the nations that come after me. Allah the Exalted granted him this, so all the people of the religions revere him and build upon him.

Al-Qutaybi said: placing "tongue" in the place of "speech" is a metaphor, because speech is described by it; and the Arabs call language a tongue. A'sha Bahila said:

"A message (lisan) came to me, which does not delight me,
from one who is exalted, not admired nor ridiculed."

﴿And make me among the heirs of the Garden of Bliss﴾. ﴿And forgive my father, for he was among those astray﴾. We have explained the reason for which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) asked forgiveness for his father in Surat al-Tawba, in a manner sufficient to avoid repeating it here.

﴿And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected﴾.

And recite to them the account of Ibrahim, when he said to his father and his people: "What do you worship?" They said: "We worship idols, and we remain devoted to them." ﴿What do you worship?﴾

Some scholars said: They said "fa-nazallu" (so we remain) because they worshipped them by day and not by night.

He said: "Do they hear you when you call (on them)?" ﴿Do they hear you when you call (on them)?﴾ The common reading (qira'a) is with a fatha on the ya', meaning: do they hear your supplication? Qatada read yusmi'unakum with a damma on the ya', meaning: do they make you hear? ﴿Or do they benefit you or harm you?﴾ They said: "No, but we found our fathers doing thus." ﴿They said: No, but we found our fathers doing thus.﴾

In this verse there is a demonstration that religion is established only by proof, and that blind imitation (taqlid) in it is invalid.

He said: "Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers, the ancients? ﴿Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers, the ancients?﴾ For they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds." ﴿For they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds.﴾ He used the singular "enemy" because the meaning of the statement is: every object of worship you have is an enemy to me, if I were to worship them on the Day of Resurrection, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They will deny their worship of them and will be opposed to them﴾.

Then he turned his face towards me and recited:

"Mix the dust with the ash and eat it,
and restrain the soul from standing in the place of asking.

If you wish to be humbled by disgrace,
then throw away what the hands of men contain."

So I left him and remained for days without entering upon him, and my longing for him grew intense. I entered upon him and was with him, but he did not speak a word. I said to him: "Why do you not speak?" He said:

"Silence in speech is forbidden, for it is the cause of perdition,
and speech contains the mines of calamities.

and when you are silent, count your body as dead."

Anas said: He lived after that for more than twenty years, not eating or drinking according to his desire.

Ja'far al-Sadiq said: ﴿And when I am ill with sins, He cures me with repentance﴾. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/111.]

Samir ibn 'Abd Allah [in the second copy: Abu 'Abd Allah said]: When the endurance of people's company makes me ill, He cures me by remembering Him and by intimacy with Him.

﴿And it is He who causes me to die, then gives me life﴾. Here "thumma" (then) is used to indicate a break and a delay.

The people of language and allusion said: He causes me to die by justice and gives me life by grace; He causes me to die by disobedience and gives me life by obedience; He causes me to die by separation and gives me life by reunion; He causes me to die by abandonment and gives me life by success; He causes me to die by wealth and gives me life by it; He causes me to die by ignorance and gives me life by knowledge.

﴿And who I hope will forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment﴾. The common reading (qira'a) is in the singular (khati'a).

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hanash related to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yazid related to us, saying: Rawh related to us, from Abu al-Yaqzan, who said: al-Hakam al-Sulami related to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan recite: "and who I hope will forgive me my sins on the Day of Judgment." He said: "It was not a single sin, but it was sins."

Mujahid and Muqatil said: they are his saying ﴿I am sick﴾, and his saying ﴿Rather, the largest of them did it﴾, and his saying to Sarah "She is my sister," al-Hasan added, and his saying about the stars ﴿This is my lord﴾.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Shadhan related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Thabit al-Hariri related to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us, saying: Abu Khalid related to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, from 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: O Messenger of Allah, 'Abd Allah ibn Jud'an used to feed the guest, maintain the ties of kinship, and free the captive; will that benefit him? He said: "No, for he never once said: 'O Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment.'"

This statement by Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is an argument against his people, and an announcement that none is fit for divinity except one who does these acts.

﴿My Lord, grant me wisdom (hukm)﴾, which is the clear explanation of a thing according to what wisdom requires. Muqatil said: understanding and knowledge; al-Kalbi said: prophethood.

﴿And join me with the righteous﴾, with those before me among the prophets in rank and station. Ibn 'Abbas said: with the people of Paradise.

﴿And make for me a tongue of truth among the later ones﴾, meaning: a good remembrance, a praiseworthy reputation, and general acceptance among the nations that come after me. Allah the Exalted granted him this, so all the people of the religions revere him and build upon him.

Al-Qutaybi said: placing "tongue" in the place of "speech" is a metaphor, because speech is described by it; and the Arabs call language a tongue. A'sha Bahila said:

"A message (lisan) came to me, which does not delight me,
from one who is exalted, not admired nor ridiculed."

﴿And make me among the heirs of the Garden of Bliss﴾. ﴿And forgive my father, for he was among those astray﴾. We have explained the reason for which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) asked forgiveness for his father in Surat al-Tawba, in a manner sufficient to avoid repeating it here.

﴿And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected﴾.

And recite to them the account of Ibrahim, when he said to his father and his people: "What do you worship?" They said: "We worship idols, and we remain devoted to them." ﴿What do you worship?﴾

Some scholars said: They said "fa-nazallu" (so we remain) because they worshipped them by day and not by night.

He said: "Do they hear you when you call (on them)?" ﴿Do they hear you when you call (on them)?﴾ The common reading (qira'a) is with a fatha on the ya', meaning: do they hear your supplication? Qatada read yusmi'unakum with a damma on the ya', meaning: do they make you hear? ﴿Or do they benefit you or harm you?﴾ They said: "No, but we found our fathers doing thus." ﴿They said: No, but we found our fathers doing thus.﴾

In this verse there is a demonstration that religion is established only by proof, and that blind imitation (taqlid) in it is invalid.

He said: "Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers, the ancients? ﴿Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers, the ancients?﴾ For they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds." ﴿For they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds.﴾ He used the singular "enemy" because the meaning of the statement is: every object of worship you have is an enemy to me, if I were to worship them on the Day of Resurrection, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They will deny their worship of them and will be opposed to them﴾.

Al-Farra' said: this is an inversion (maqlub); he meant: "I am their enemy," because whoever you oppose opposes you.

Then He said: "except the Lord of the worlds," which is in the accusative by way of exception, meaning: they are an enemy to me, and what is not worshipped by me, except the Lord of the worlds, for I worship Him. This is what al-Farra' said. It was also said that it means "but" (lakin). Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: meaning the matter is with the Lord of the worlds.

Then He described Him, saying: ﴿Who created me, and it is He who guides me﴾. He informed that the true guide is the Creator, and there is no guide other than Him.

The people of language (ahl al-lisan) said: ﴿Who created me﴾ in this world upon His natural disposition (fitra), ﴿and it is He who guides me﴾ in the Hereafter to His Garden.

﴿And who feeds me and gives me drink﴾, meaning: who provides for me and nurtures me.

Abu al-'Abbas ibn 'Ata' said: meaning He feeds me whatever food He wills, and gives me to drink whatever drink He wills.

Muhammad ibn Kathir al-'Abdi said: I accompanied Sufyan al-Thawri in Mecca for a long time, and he would sip from Saturday to Saturday a handful of sand.

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: I heard Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Shah say: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Hamdan say: I heard al-Hajjaj ibn 'Abd al-Karim say:

I left Balkh seeking Ibrahim ibn Adham, and I found him in Hims in a kiln which he was heating. I greeted him and asked about his condition, and he returned my greeting and asked me about my condition and the condition of my relatives. I stayed with him that day, and he said: "Perhaps your soul urges you towards some food?" I said: "Yes." So he took ashes and dust, mixed them together, and ate them. Then he turned his face towards me and recited:

"Mix the dust with the ash and eat it,
and restrain the soul from standing in the place of asking.

If you wish to be humbled by disgrace,
then throw away what the hands of men contain."

So I left him and remained for days without entering upon him, and my longing for him grew intense. I entered upon him and was with him, but he did not speak a word. I said to him: "Why do you not speak?" He said:

"Silence in speech is forbidden, for it is the cause of perdition,
and speech contains the mines of calamities.

So when you speak, be mindful of your Lord,
and when you are silent, count your body as dead."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "﴿Who feeds me﴾ without food, and ﴿gives me drink﴾ without drink." Its figurative meaning is: He satisfies me and quenches me without any intermediary, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I pass the night being fed by my Lord and given drink by Him."

This is shown by the hadith of the water-carrier in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), when he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) recite for three days: ﴿There is no creature on earth but that its provision is upon Allah﴾, and he threw away his waterskin. Then someone came to him in a dream with a cup of the drink of Paradise and gave him to drink.

Anas said: He lived after that for more than twenty years, not eating or drinking according to his desire.

Ali ibn Qadim said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Na'm would not eat more than once a month. This reached al-Hajjaj, who summoned him, placed him in a house, and locked its door. He opened it after fifteen days, not doubting that he had died, and found him standing and praying. He said: "O wicked one, you pray without ablution!" He replied: "Only one who eats and drinks needs ablution, and I am in the state of purity into which you placed me in this house."

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Naysaburi say: I heard Abu Nasr Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah al-Isfahani say: I heard Abu Sa'id al-Kharraz in Mecca say: I was hungry in Tarsus, and my hunger intensified, so I sat on the bank of the river and placed my feet in the water, and I was called: "Are you weary of your hunger? Take the satiety of eternity."

He said: So he lived after that for years without desiring food or drink, yet whenever he wished to eat or drink, he was able to.

It reached me that a woman was taken captive from Aleppo to the Byzantines in the days of Sayf al-Dawla 'Ali ibn Hamdan. She escaped from them and walked two hundred farsakh without eating anything. She came to Sayf al-Dawla, and he said to her: "How were you able to walk, and how did you live without food?" She said: "Whenever I was hungry or exhausted, I recited ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ three times, and I was satisfied, quenched and strengthened."

I heard Abu al-Qasim say: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Nasrabadi say: I heard Abu Bakr al-Shibli say: There is a subtlety in bread that satisfies you, not the bread itself. Had He willed, He would have left that subtlety in you so that you would not need bread.

Dhu al-Nun al-Misri said: "He feeds me the food of love and gives me to drink the drink of love." Then he recited:

"The drink of love is the best of drinks,
and every other drink is a mirage."

I heard Ibn Habib say: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Jurjani say: I heard al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiyya al-Damghani say [in the second copy there is an addition: Abu al-Qasim said: he heard my father say: I heard 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Warraq say: I heard my uncle say]: I heard my uncle say: I heard Abu Yazid al-Bistami say: Indeed Allah has a drink called the drink of love, which He has stored up for His most excellent servants. When they drink it, they become intoxicated; when they are intoxicated, they become senseless; when they are senseless, they fly; when they fly, they arrive; and when they arrive, they are joined. They are ﴿in a seat of truth, in the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful﴾.

Al-Junayd said: People will be gathered all naked, except those who wore the garment of piety; and hungry, except those who ate the food of gnosis (ma'rifa); and thirsty, except those who drank the drink of love.

﴿And when I am ill﴾: Ibrahim (peace be upon him) attributed the illness to himself, though it is from Allah the Exalted, because his people regarded it as a defect, so he employed good manners. Similar to this is the story of al-Khidr, when he said: ﴿So I intended to damage it﴾, and he said: ﴿So your Lord intended that they should reach their maturity﴾.

﴿And it is He who cures me﴾, meaning: heals me. It is related that Abu Bakr al-Warraq passed by a physician who was giving medicines to people, so he stopped by him and said: "Does your medicine do two things?" He said: "And what are they?" He said: "Reverse the decree of a judge and bring about the cure of one who cures?" He said: "No." He said: "Then it is not [anything]."

Ja'far al-Sadiq said: ﴿And when I am ill with sins, He cures me with repentance﴾. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/111.]

Samir ibn 'Abd Allah [in the second copy: Abu 'Abd Allah said]: When the endurance of people's company makes me ill, He cures me by remembering Him and by intimacy with Him.

﴿And it is He who causes me to die, then gives me life﴾. Here "thumma" (then) is used to indicate a break and a delay.

The people of language and allusion said: He causes me to die by justice and gives me life by grace; He causes me to die by disobedience and gives me life by obedience; He causes me to die by separation and gives me life by reunion; He causes me to die by abandonment and gives me life by success; He causes me to die by wealth and gives me life by it; He causes me to die by ignorance and gives me life by knowledge.

﴿And who I hope will forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment﴾. The common reading (qira'a) is in the singular (khati'a).

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hanash related to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yazid related to us, saying: Rawh related to us, from Abu al-Yaqzan, who said: al-Hakam al-Sulami related to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan recite: "and who I hope will forgive me my sins on the Day of Judgment." He said: "It was not a single sin, but it was sins."

Mujahid and Muqatil said: they are his saying ﴿I am sick﴾, and his saying ﴿Rather, the largest of them did it﴾, and his saying to Sarah "She is my sister," al-Hasan added, and his saying about the stars ﴿This is my lord﴾.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Shadhan related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Thabit al-Hariri related to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us, saying: Abu Khalid related to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, from 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: O Messenger of Allah, 'Abd Allah ibn Jud'an used to feed the guest, maintain the ties of kinship, and free the captive; will that benefit him? He said: "No, for he never once said: 'O Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment.'"

﴿And join me with the righteous﴾, with those before me among the prophets in rank and station. Ibn 'Abbas said: with the people of Paradise.

﴿And make for me a tongue of truth among the later ones﴾, meaning: a good remembrance, a praiseworthy reputation, and general acceptance among the nations that come after me. Allah the Exalted granted him this, so all the people of the religions revere him and build upon him.

"A message (lisan) came to me, which does not delight me,
from one who is exalted, not admired nor ridiculed."

﴿And make me among the heirs of the Garden of Bliss﴾. ﴿And forgive my father, for he was among those astray﴾. We have explained the reason for which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) asked forgiveness for his father in Surat al-Tawba, in a manner sufficient to avoid repeating it here.

﴿And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected﴾.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 26, verses 88–104:

﴿The day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, except one who comes to God with a sound heart﴾, sound and free of association (shirk) and doubt. As for sins, no one is free of them. This is the view of most of the commentators.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: The sound heart is the healthy heart, which is the heart of the believer, because the heart of the disbeliever and the hypocrite is diseased. God, glorified is He, said: ﴿in their hearts is a disease﴾ [Qur'an 2:10].

Abu 'Uthman al-Naysaburi said: It is the heart that is empty of innovation (bid'ah) and at peace with the Sunnah.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: It is sound from the affliction of wealth and children.

Al-Junayd said: In the language, *salim* means *al-ladigh* (the one who has been stung), so its meaning is like one stung by the fear of God.

﴿And Paradise was brought near﴾, that is, drawn close, for the God-fearing. ﴿And Hellfire was made manifest﴾, that is, made visible, for the deviators ﴿al-ghawin﴾, that is, for the disbelievers. ﴿And it will be said to them on the Day of Resurrection: Where is what you used to worship besides God? Can they help you, or can they help themselves?﴾ ﴿Then they will be thrown into it, they and the deviators﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: *fa-kubkibu* means they were gathered together. Mujahid said: they went away. Muqatil said: they were hurled. Its root is *kubbibu*, and the letter *kaf* was repeated in it, like your saying *tahannahani* and *rih sarsar* and similar forms.

﴿they and the deviators﴾, meaning the devils, according to Qatadah and Muqatil. Al-Kalbi said: they are the disbelieving jinn.

﴿And the hosts of Iblis, all of them﴾, that is, his followers and those who obeyed him among the jinn and mankind. They will say to the devils and the worshipped ones: ﴿By God, we were certainly in clear error, when we equated you with the Lord of the worlds﴾, that is, we made you equal to Him, so we worshipped you besides Him. ﴿And none led us astray except the criminals﴾, meaning the devils, according to Muqatil and al-Kalbi. That is, they called us to error and commanded us to it. Abu al-'Aliyah and 'Ikrimah said: it means Iblis and the son of Adam who killed, because he was the first to establish fighting and various kinds of sin.

﴿So we have no intercessors, nor a close friend﴾, a near one who would benefit us and intercede for us. That will be when the angels, the prophets and the believers intercede.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Fanjuwi informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Yaqtini related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-'Uqayli informed us, saying: Safwan ibn Salih related to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, saying: It was related to us by one who heard Abu al-Zubayr say: I bear witness that I heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Indeed, a man will say in Paradise: My Lord, what has happened to my friend so-and-so? And his friend is in the Blazing Fire. God, glorified is He, will say: Bring out his friend to Paradise. Then the one who remains will say: ﴿So we have no intercessors, nor a close friend﴾" [Zad al-Masir 6/43] [96].

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah related to us, saying: Sam'an ibn Abi Mas'ud related to us, saying: al-Mada' ibn al-Jarud related to us, saying: Salih al-Murri related to us, from al-Hasan, who said: No assembly gathers in the remembrance of God, the Exalted, among whom is a servant from the people of Paradise, except that God will allow him to intercede for them. The people of faith intercede for one another, and they are, with God, interceders and those whose intercession is accepted.

﴿So if only we had a return (karrah) to the world﴾, they will wish, when it no longer benefits them, ﴿that we might be among the believers﴾. ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers. And indeed, your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: The sound heart is the healthy heart, which is the heart of the believer, because the heart of the disbeliever and the hypocrite is diseased. God, glorified is He, said: ﴿in their hearts is a disease﴾ [Qur'an 2:10].

Abu 'Uthman al-Naysaburi said: It is the heart that is empty of innovation (bid'ah) and at peace with the Sunnah.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: It is sound from the affliction of wealth and children.

Al-Junayd said: In the language, *salim* means *al-ladigh* (the one who has been stung), so its meaning is like one stung by the fear of God.

﴿And Paradise was brought near﴾, that is, drawn close, for the God-fearing. ﴿And Hellfire was made manifest﴾, that is, made visible, for the deviators ﴿al-ghawin﴾, that is, for the disbelievers. ﴿And it will be said to them on the Day of Resurrection: Where is what you used to worship besides God? Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 26, verse 105–122:

كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ (The people of Noah denied) — the feminine verb (kadhdhabat) is used here for a group (jama'ah), like His saying: ﴿The Bedouins said﴾ (qalat al-a'rabu).

الْمُرْسَلِينَ (the messengers) — meaning Noah alone, like His saying: ﴿O messengers﴾ [[Surat al-Mu'minun: 51.]].

And Abu 'Abd Allah al-Dinawari informed me, saying: Abu 'Ali al-Maqri narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Ubayd 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Harb narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sabbah narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Isma'il, from al-Husayn, who said: It was said to him: "O Abu Sa'id, what do you say about the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers﴾ [[Surat al-Shu'ara': 123.]], ﴿'Ad denied the messengers﴾ [[Surat al-Shu'ara': 123.]], ﴿Thamud denied the messengers﴾ [[Surat al-Shu'ara': 141.]], when they were sent only one messenger each?"

He said: "The latter came with what the former came with, so when they denied one, they denied them all."

إِذْ قالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ (When their brother said to them) — in lineage, not in religion — نُوحٌ (Noah): ﴿Will you not fear God? Ibn 'Abbas said: the weavers (al-hakah) [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/24; Zad al-Masir: 6/44.]].

And al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Fanjawi informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Ka'bi narrated to us, saying: Husayn [[In the second copy: al-Ka'bi from Hasun ibn al-Haytham al-Ruwayzi, who said: Abu 'Ali informed me, from Muhammad ibn Bukayr ibn Marwan al-Fihri, from his father, from al-Dahhak.]] ibn Muzahim narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the saying of God, glorified is He: ﴿And the lowest follow you﴾; he said: the weavers. 'Ikrimah said: the weavers and the tanners (al-asalifah).

إِنْ حِسابُهُمْ إِلَّا عَلى رَبِّي لَوْ تَشْعُرُونَ (Their reckoning is only upon my Lord, if you were aware). It has also been said: its meaning is, I did not know that God guides them and misguides you, grants them success and forsakes you.

Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil said: among the killed.

قالَ نوح (Noah said): ﴿And what is my knowledge of what they used to do?﴾ Indeed, for me is only their outward affair, and it is incumbent upon me to call them; nothing is upon me of the lowliness of their conditions or the baseness of their livelihoods. I was not charged with that; I was charged only with calling them.

إِنْ حِسابُهُمْ إِلَّا عَلى رَبِّي لَوْ تَشْعُرُونَ (Their reckoning is only upon my Lord, if you were aware). It has also been said: its meaning is, I did not know that God guides them and misguides you, grants them success and forsakes you.

وَما أَنَا بِطارِدِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِنْ أَنَا إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ (And I am not one to drive away the believers; I am only a clear warner). قالُوا لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهِ يا نُوحُ (They said: "If you do not desist, O Noah,") عمّا تقول وتدعو إليه (from what you say and call to), لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمَرْجُومِينَ (you will surely be among the stoned). It means the cursed (al-mash'umin), according to al-Dahhak; Qatadah said: those struck with stones.

Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil said: among the killed.

al-Thumali said: every mention of al-marjumin in the Qur'an means killing, except the one in Surat Maryam: ﴿If you do not desist, I will surely stone you (la-arjumannaka)﴾ [[Surat Maryam: 46.]], where it means I will revile you.

قالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ قَوْمِي كَذَّبُونِ (He said: "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me.") فَافْتَحْ (So judge) — fāftaḥ, meaning: decide — بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُمْ فَتْحاً وَنَجِّنِي وَمَنْ مَعِيَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (between me and them with a judgment, and save me and those of the believers who are with me). فَأَنْجَيْناهُ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ فِي الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونِ (So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship). al-Mashhun means the loaded and equipped, according to Ibn 'Abbas. Mujahid: the filled, the completed; 'Ata': the weighed down; Qatadah: the carrying.

Then We drowned the rest. Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. And indeed your Lord – He is the Mighty, the Merciful.

The people of ʿAd denied the messengers when their brother Hud said to them, "Will you not fear God? Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you, so fear God and obey me. And I do not ask you any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds."

Al-Kalbi said: "Trustworthy" (amin) means trustworthy in conveying the message. And al-Kalbi said: trustworthy among you before the message, so how can you accuse me today?

"Do you build on every high place (rīʿ) a landmark, sporting?"

Al-Walibi related from Ibn ʿAbbas: "Every high place (rīʿ)."

Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: "A road." This is the narration of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Ibn Jurayj related from Mujahid: It is the mountain pass between two mountains.

Ibn Abi Najih related from him: It is a small opening. And also from him, ʿIkrimah said: a valley.

Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: They used to travel and were not guided except by the stars, so they built long towers on the roads, uselessly, so that they might be guided by them. What indicates this is His saying, "a sign" (āyah), meaning a landmark.

It is also related from Mujahid, who said: rīʿ is the building of pigeon-houses. Its evidence is His saying, "sporting" (tabathūn), meaning playing. Abu ʿUbayd said: it is an elevated place, and he recited the verse of Dhu al-Rummah:

"The fledgling's wings spread over its elevation, dew of a night glistening in its feathers."

There are two dialects: rīʿ and rīʿ, with the rāʾ vowelled with kasra and with fatha, and its plural is aryāʿ and its diminutive is ruyayʿah.

"And you take for yourselves palaces (maṣāniʿ)."

Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid said: lofty palaces. Maʿmar related from him: fortresses.

Ibn Abi Najih related from him: pigeon towers. Qatadah: reservoirs for water. Al-Kalbi: dwellings. ʿAbd al-Razzaq: "Among us, in the language of Yemen, maṣāniʿ means ancient palaces; its singular is maṣniʿ."

"Perhaps you will abide forever (takhludūn)."

Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah said: that is, as if you would remain in them forever. Ibn Zayd said: laʿalla is interrogative, meaning, "Will you abide forever when you build these things?" Al-Farra' said: "so that you may abide forever."

"And when you seize (baṭashtum), that is, you strike with force and seize, [you seize] as tyrants (jabbārīn), killers without right."

Mujahid said: killing by the sword and striking with the whip. The jabbār is one who kills and strikes in anger.

"So fear God and obey me, and fear Him who has aided you with what you know."

Then he mentioned what He had given them, saying, "He has aided you with cattle and children, gardens and springs. Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day."

They said, "It is all the same to us whether you admonish or are not among the admonishers. This is only the custom of the ancients."

Al-ʿAbbas related from Ibn ʿUmayr, and Waqid from al-Kisa'i, the assimilation of the ṭāʾ into the tāʾ (idghām); the rest read with clear pronunciation (idhhār), which is the preferred reading.

Abu Jaʿfar, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, Yaʿqub, Ayyub, Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim read khuluq with a fatha on the khāʾ, due to His saying, "and you fabricate a falsehood" (takhluqūna ifkan), and His saying, "This is only fabrication" (ikhtilaq). Its meaning: "This is only the practice of the ancients and their myths and their tales." The rest read it with a ḍammah on the khāʾ and the lām, meaning the worship of the ancients before us, who live as long as they live and then die, with no resurrection and no reckoning. This is the interpretation of Qatadah.

﴿Thamud denied the messengers when their brother Salih said to them: "Will you not fear God? I am a trustworthy messenger to you. So fear God and obey me. I ask you for no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds. Will you be left secure in what is here," that is, in this world, "among gardens and springs, and fields and palm trees whose spathes are soft (talʿuhā, its fruit), HAḌĪM"﴾ [[Source footnotes are not reproduced here.]]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Ḥaḍīm means delicate, as long as it is in its kifrā," meaning its sheath or covering (duʿāʾuhu). From this comes the saying "ḥaḍīm al-kashḥ" (slender of waist), when someone is slender, and "ḥaḍama al-ṭaʿām" (the food was digested) when it became fine and changed into its own form. ʿAṭiyyah related from him: "Yāniʿ, ripe." Qatadah and ʿIkrimah: "Soft dates." al-Ḥasan: "Loose and tender."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Mahan narrated to us, saying: al-Ṭanāfisī narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Salam, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-ʿAla', regarding ﴿its spathes are HAḌĪM﴾, he said: "Mudhannab (having a tail-like fault)." Mujahid: "Mutahashshim mutafattit (crumbling and brittle), and that is when it emerges, it overflows upon it and digests it. As long as it is moist it is ḥaḍīm, and when it dries it is hashīm." Abu al-ʿĀliyah: "Yuhashhish in the mouth (it melts in the mouth)." al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Muqatil: "Piled up, one part resting upon another until they crush one another; its root is from breaking."

﴿And you carve out houses from the mountains, FĀRIHĪN﴾. The people of Syria and Kufa read ﴿fārihīn﴾ with an alif, which is the reading of the companions of ʿAbd Allah (Ibn Masʿud) and the choice of Abu ʿUbayd, meaning "skilful in choosing them." ʿAṭiyyah and ʿAbd Allah ibn Shaddad said: "Choosing the places for carving." The rest read ﴿farihīn﴾ without an alif, which is the choice of Abu Ḥatim. They differed on its meaning. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Ashirīn (insolent, exultant)." al-Ḍaḥḥāk: "Clever (kayyisīn)." Qatadah: "Admiring your craftsmanship." Mujahid: "Greedy (sharahīn)." ʿIkrimah: "Pampered (nāʿimīn)." al-Suddi: "Bewildered (mutaḥayyirīn)." Ibn Zayd: "Strong (aqwiyāʾ)." al-Kisa'i: "Haughty (baṭirīn)." Abu ʿUbaydah and al-Akhfash: "Joyful (faraḥīn)." The Arabs interchange the ḥāʾ and the hāʾ, as in "madaḥtuhu" and "madahtuhu" (I praised him). It is also permissible that ﴿farihīn﴾ and ﴿fārihīn﴾ have one meaning, like His words ﴿ʿiẓāman nakhirah﴾ (bones, decayed) [Q. 79:11], and "nākhirah" and the like.

﴿So fear God and obey me, and do not obey the command of the MUSRIFĪN﴾, the polytheists, ﴿who spread corruption in the land and do not set things right.﴾ They said: ﴿You are only one of the MUSAḤḤARĪN﴾, that is, the bewitched, the deceived, according to Mujahid and Qatadah.

al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih from Ibn ʿAbbas: "Those who are fed and given drink (muʿallalīn bi al-ṭaʿām wa al-sharāb)." al-Kalbi recited the verse of Labid:

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Ḥaḍīm means delicate, as long as it is in its kifrā," meaning its sheath or covering (duʿāʾuhu). Qatadah and ʿIkrimah: "Soft dates." al-Ḥasan: "Loose and tender."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Mahan narrated to us, saying: al-Ṭanāfisī narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Salam, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-ʿAla', regarding ﴿its spathes are HAḌĪM﴾, he said: "Mudhannab (having a tail-like fault)." ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you. So fear God and obey me. And I do not ask you any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ The wording of these prophets, as God the Exalted related it about them, is in one single form, to inform that the truth to which they call is one, and that they agreed on the command to piety, obedience, sincerity in worship, and refraining from taking payment for the call and the conveying of the message.

﴿Give full measure, and do not be among the losers﴾, meaning those who give short measure and weight.

﴿And weigh with a balance that is straight. And do not deprive people of their things, and do not spread corruption in the earth, causing mischief. And fear Him who created you and the former generations (al-jibilla).﴾ Al-jibbil means creation. The poet said:

"Death is the greatest of events / among those that pass over the creation (al-jibilla)."

﴿They said: "You are only one of those bewitched. You are only a human like us, and we think you are surely among the liars. So cause a piece of the sky to fall upon us, if you are of the truthful."﴾ He said: ﴿"My Lord knows best what you do,"﴾ meaning He will repay you for it. ﴿And my duty is only to convey the message.﴾

﴿So they denied him, and the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them.﴾ The reason was that God the Exalted withheld the wind from them for seven days and sent heat upon them until it took their breaths, and neither shade nor water benefited them. They used to enter the caves to cool themselves in them, but when they entered them they found them hotter than the outside, so they fled into the wilderness, and a cloud overshadowed them, which is the "canopy." They found coolness and a breeze in it, so some of them called to others, until, when they gathered beneath it, it rained fire upon them and they were burned.

Qatada said: God the Exalted sent Shu'ayb to two nations: the companions of the Thicket and the people of Madyan. As for the companions of the Thicket, they were destroyed by the canopy, and as for the people of Madyan, the Blast seized them; Jibril cried out at them with one cry and they all perished.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Alawayh related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Isa related to us, saying: al-Musayyab related to us, from Barad al-Jurayri, who said: The heat was made to rule over them for seven days and nights. Then a mountain was raised for them from afar, and a man of them came to it, and beneath it were rivers, springs and cold water. He settled beneath it and took what sufficed him, then went to his household and informed them, and they came and took what sufficed them and settled. Then he informed the rest of the people, and they all gathered beneath it, and it did not leave any of them behind, and that mountain fell upon them. That is His saying: ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. Indeed it was the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾

Those of the Thicket (al-Ayka) denied the Messengers. The Thicket is a dense grove (al-ghaydha), and they were the people of Shu'ayb. Both "al-Layka" and "al-Ayka" are dialectal forms, and both have been recited.

And truly it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. That is, the Qur'an. The Trustworthy Spirit (al-Ruh al-Amin) has brought it down. The people of the Hijaz and Abu 'Amr read nazzala with a light zay and with raf' (nominative) on the ha' and nun, meaning Jibril (peace be upon him) with the Qur'an. The others read it with a heavy zay and with fath (accusative) on the ha' and nun, meaning God sent down (nazzala) Jibril (peace be upon him). This is the preference of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim, because of His saying "and truly it is a revelation (tanzil)," which is a verbal noun of nazzala, upon your heart, O Muhammad, so that you may memorize it.

So that you may be among the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue. That is, it was sent down in a clear Arabic tongue. And truly it, that is, the mention of the Qur'an and its report, is in the Books of the Ancients (zubur). According to the majority of the exegetes. Muqatil said: that is, the mention of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his description. Al-A'mash read zubri with a sukun on the ba', and others with a damma.

Has it not been a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it? Ibn 'Amir read takun with a ta' and ayatun with a raf' (damma). Others read takun with a ta' and ayatan with a nasb (fatha). The meaning of the verse: Is it not a proof and a sign for these deniers that the scholars of the Children of Israel know him, that is, Muhammad? They are 'Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions. Ibn 'Abbas said: The people of Makkah sent to the Jews, who were in Madinah, and asked them about Muhammad (ﷺ). They said: "Indeed, this is his time, and we find his description and his attributes in the Torah." That was a sign for them of his truthfulness.

And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs (a'jamin). A'jam is the plural of a'jam, one who does not speak clearly and does not speak Arabic well, even if he is ascribed to the Arabs. Its feminine is 'ajma', and its plural is 'ajam. From it, beasts are called 'ajam, because they do not speak. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The wound of the beast (al-'ajma') is a wasted claim." [Musnad Ahmad: 2/254.] If you want to say that it is ascribed to the non-Arabs (al-'Ajam), you say: 'ajami.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hanash told us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl told us, saying: Sahl ibn 'Ali told us, saying: Abu 'Amr told us, saying: Shuja' ibn Abi Nasr told us, from 'Isa ibn 'Umar, from al-Hasan, that he read "wa law nazzalnahu 'ala ba'di al-a'jamiyyin" with a shadda on two yas, making it a nisba. The meaning of the verse: And if We had sent it down upon a man who is not Arabic in tongue, and he had recited it to them in a language other than the language of the Arabs, they would still not have believed in it. They would have said, "We do not understand your speech." Its parallel is His saying, "And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said, 'Why have its verses not been explained?'" [Surah Fussilat: 44.] It is also said that the meaning is: if We had sent it down upon a man who is not from the Arabs, they would not have believed in it out of arrogance from following him.

Thus We have caused it to enter into the hearts of the criminals, that is, We caused the Qur'an to enter their hearts so that the proof would be established against them. It is also said: that is, We caused disbelief to enter the hearts of the criminals, so they do not believe in it.

Al-Farra' said: It is the custom of the Arabs, when they put la in the place of kay in such a context, that they sometimes jussify what follows and sometimes raise it. You say: "I tied the horse, la yanfalit," with jazm and raf'. And "I bound the slave, la ya'biq," in the jazm, under the interpretation: if I do not tie him, he will escape; and if I do not bind him, he will flee. The raf' is on the basis that the jazim is not apparent. A man from the Banu 'Aqil recited:

"Until we saw the best of goodwill between us
Dwelling, which the evil doer does not sully."

He recites it with raf' and jazm. And from the jazm is the saying of the rajiz:

"How long you have driven her away, so she does not return,
So leave her, and the water-draw cools."

Until they see the painful punishment, and it will come upon them suddenly. The common reading is with the ya', meaning the punishment.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hanash told us, saying: Abu al-'Abbas 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Hammad al-Tahrani informed us, saying: Abu Zakariyya Yahya ibn al-Fadl al-Harami informed us, saying: Wahb ibn 'Amr al-Namari told us, saying: Harun ibn Musa al-'Ataki informed us, saying: al-Hussam told us, from al-Hasan, that he read "fa-ya'tiyahum baghtatan" with a ta'. A man said to him: "O Abu Sa'id, the punishment only comes upon them suddenly." Al-Hasan rebuked him and said: "It is only the Hour."

And they do not perceive, so that they will say: "Are we to be reprieved?"

Muqatil said: The polytheists said: "O Muhammad, until when will you threaten us with the punishment?" So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "Do they then seek to hasten Our punishment? Have you considered, if We let them enjoy for years," in this world, and We do not destroy them, "then there comes to them what they were promised," meaning the punishment, "what they were given enjoyment of will not avail them." "And We did not destroy any town except that it had warners," messengers who warned them, "as a reminder," that is, they warned them as a reminder. Its place is accusative; it is also said it is nominative, meaning: that is a reminder. "And We were not wrongdoers," in punishing them, since We had sent forth the proof against them and given them excuse.

And the devils have not brought it down. Rather, the Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down. The common reading is ash-shayatin with a ya' throughout the Qur'an, because its nun is original and its spelling is one, like al-dahaqin and al-basatin.

Al-Hasan al-Basri and Muhammad ibn al-Sumaydah al-Yamani read ash-shayatun with a waw. Al-Farra' said: The shaykh (meaning al-Hasan) erred. It was said: That is al-Nadr ibn Shumayl. It was said: If it is permissible to argue with the speech of al-'Ajjaj and Ru'ba and those below them, why is it not permissible to argue with the speech of al-Hasan and his companion? Yet we know that they did not recite it except that they had heard it.

The historian said: If the derivation of ash-shayatin is from shaṭa yashiṭu, then their reading would have a basis.

Ibn Shabbah informed me, saying: I heard Abu 'Ubayd say: We did not criticize al-Hasan in his recitation except for his saying: "wa ma tanazzalat bihi ash-shayatun."

With his chain, from 'Umar ibn Shabbah, who said: Abu Harb al-Babi, of the descendants of Bab, told us, saying: A Bedouin came to Yunus ibn Habib and said: "A young man of your youths came to us, brought us to this pond, and seated us in a wooden two-winged thing, then led us into gardens behind which were gardens (basatun)."

Yunus said: "This resembles the recitation of al-Hasan."

And it is not fitting for them (to bring it down), nor are they able to do so. Indeed, they are removed from the hearing, that is, from eavesdropping on the heaven, and are pelted with meteors. So do not call upon another god with God, lest you be among the punished. And warn your tribe, the nearest kin.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abdullah told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Shabib al-Mu'ammar told us, saying: 'Abbad ibn Ya'qub told me, saying: 'Ali ibn Hashim told us, from Sabbah ibn Yahya al-Muzanni, from Zakariyya ibn Maysara, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: When "And warn your tribe, the nearest kin" was revealed, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gathered the sons of 'Abd al-Muttalib, and they were then forty men, each of whom would eat a whole sheep and drink a large bowl. He commanded 'Ali with a leg of sheep, which he prepared, then said: "Come forward in the name of God." The people came forward ten by ten, and they ate until they were satisfied. Then he called for a bowl of milk, took a sip from it, and said to them: "Drink in the name of God." The people drank until they were quenched. Abu Lahab forestalled them and said: "This is what the man has bewitched you with." The Prophet (ﷺ) was silent that day and did not speak.

Then the next day he invited them to the same food and drink, and then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) warned them, saying: "O sons of 'Abd al-Muttalib, I am the warner to you from God, Glorified, and the bearer of good news of what none of you has come with. I have come to you with this world and the Hereafter, so submit and obey me, and you will be guided. Who will be my brother, my supporter, my heir and my successor after me, and the one who will fulfill my debt?" The people were silent, and he repeated this three times, and every time the people were silent, while 'Ali said: "I." He said: "You." The people rose, saying to Abu Talib: "Obey your son, for he has been made your commander." [Shawahid al-Tanzil – al-Haskani: 1/543.]

And 'Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Hamdun informed us, both saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abu al-Yaman told us, saying: Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: The Prophet (ﷺ) stood when God, Glorified, revealed "And warn your tribe, the nearest kin," and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, buy yourselves from God; I cannot avail you anything against God. O sons of 'Abd Manaf, I cannot avail you anything against God. O 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, I cannot avail you anything against God. O Fatimah daughter of Muhammad, I cannot avail you anything against God. O Safiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of God, I cannot avail you anything against God. Ask me from my wealth whatever you wish." [Kanz al-'Ummal: 16/9.]

And 'Abdullah ibn Hamid informed me, saying: Makki ibn 'Abdan informed us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Hashim told us, saying: 'Abdullah told us, saying: al-A'mash told us, from 'Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When God, Glorified, revealed "And warn your tribe, the nearest kin," the Messenger of God (ﷺ) went up to al-Safa, climbed upon it, and called out "Ya sabahah!" The people gathered to him, some coming and some sending a messenger. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "O sons of 'Abd al-Muttalib, O sons of Fihr, if I told you that cavalry at the foot of this mountain wanted to raid you, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "May you perish for the rest of this day! Did you call us only for this?" So God revealed: "Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he." [Musnad Ahmad: 1/307.]

And lower your wing to those among the believers who follow you. That is, soften your side for those who follow you. But if they disobey you, say: "I am innocent of what you do," namely, of worshipping idols and disobeying the Most Merciful.

So put your trust (fa-tawakkal), with the fa', in the Medinans and the Syrians, and so it is in their codices; the others read it with the waw (wa-tawakkal), meaning and put your trust in the Mighty, the Merciful, that He may suffice you against the plots of your enemies.

Who sees you when you stand

to your prayer, according to most of the exegetes.

Mujahid said: "Who sees you" wherever you are, "and your turning" and He sees your turning in your prayer, in your standing, sitting, bowing and prostration.

'Ikrimah and 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, said, and Mujahid said: "and sees your turning among those who pray," that is, your seeing those who are behind you as you see those who are in front of you. He said: He used to see from behind him as he saw in front of him.

'Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: al-Sulami, Ahmad ibn Hafs, 'Abdullah al-Farra', and Qatan told us, saying: Hafs told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Tahman told us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Complete the bowing and the prostration, for by God, I see you from behind my back when you bow and prostrate." [Musnad Abi Ya'la: 5/464.]

Qatadah, Ibn Zayd, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: that is, your movement among those who pray in the pillars of the prayer in congregation, standing, sitting, bowing and prostrating. This is also the narration of 'Ata' al-Khurasani from Ibn 'Abbas.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: and your movement in your states, as the prophets before you used to do, and "those who prostrate" in this view are the prophets.

Al-Hasan said: that is, your movement, your going and coming among your companions and the believers.

Abu Sahl 'Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Habib al-Muqri informed me, saying: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Musa told us, saying: Zanjawayh ibn Muhammad told us, saying: 'Ali ibn Sa'id al-Nasawi Abu 'Asim told us, from Suhayb, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding "and your movement among those who prostrate": from one prophet to another, until I brought you forth in this nation.

"Until we saw the best of goodwill between us
Dwelling, which the evil doer does not sully."
